newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks open firm, focus on second liners.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks open firm, focus on second liners.

text.p: Singapore shares were firmer at the open on Monday with focus on second liners and Malaysian over-the-counter (OTC) issues.
Dealers said the market's undertone was firm and ignored the weaker close of Wall Street stocks on Friday.
"The play is still on the OTCs which took a breather last week. Singapore small cap stocks are also moving," said a dealer with a local firm.
After 40 minutes of trading, the benchmark Straits Times Industrial index was up 6.11 points to 2,201.81 while the UOB-OTC index was up 5.50 points to 1,352.02.

Among the most active was infrastructure company Wee Poh, which reached a new high of S$0.99, up 2.5 cents. The company had issued just under 25 million shares in its initial public offer late last year.

Interiors firm Nobel Design also touched a new high of S$0.985, up 4.5 cents in active dealings. "The stocks are being pushed up. It is easy to do so because of the small number of shares in issue," said a dealer.
Blue chips like OCBC foreign, Cycle & Carriage and Keppel Corp saw some light buying moving up between 10 to 30 cents each. - Doreen Siow 65-8703092 REUTER
